name: blueprint/governed-exec
description: Every high-impact command as a governed, receipted step: guard rules gate the prefix, rh_run executes with bounded collected output, and the store keeps a before/after receipt (the undo trail). What the tool guard does per call, this blueprint does per task.
use_cases: tidy folders with an undo trail
ingredients: rh_run / rh_run_bg (argv array, no shell interpretation)
guard rules (config: toolPrefix + mode allow/deny/ask + destructive marker)
rh_store receipts: { argv, cwd, exitCode, at } and before/after undo pairs
recipe: gate the prefix with a guard rule -> write the before-receipt -> rh_run (collect mode when the output matters) -> write the after-receipt with exit code and a one-line summary -> revert = read the receipt and move each { to -> from } in reverse
result_kind: one receipt key per command plus an undo trail for mutating steps

invoke_contract.revert: read receipt -> reverse each recorded mutation

config_variants.gate: none | deny destructive prefixes | ask with a policy function
config_variants.journal: receipts only | full before/after undo pairs

pitfalls: rh_run is collect mode and bounded - the output you need must fit the cap; rh_run_bg reports status/exit but not captured stdout (live-verified)
argv arrays only - shell operators, pipes and redirects are the caller's job
a deny rule fires BEFORE dispatch; an ask rule defers to the policy function
the destructive marker documents why a prefix is gated but never changes enforcement
golden-file the derived facts (UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 pnpm test) so a guard change is a visible diff, not a surprise
local_limits: undo quality equals receipt quality - a mutation not recorded cannot be reverted
cloud_limits: remote commands (wrangler deploy) need the user's Cloudflare credentials; the auth gate is rh_credential_describe first
